subject: Physics + Chemistry + Biology
schema_note: Keyed by topic_id (matches neet_syllabus.json). Fields: concepts, formulas, methods, traps, hard_archetypes, banned_easy_templates, out_of_scope. NEET is single-correct MCQ only, so 'hard_archetypes' describes trickier single-correct item designs (multi-step reasoning, ranking/comparison, graph/diagram interpretation) rather than multi-part JEE-style problems.

concepts: Fundamental vs derived units
Significant figures and rules of rounding
Dimensional homogeneity
formulas: [X] = M^a L^b T^c form of dimensional formula
Error propagation: relative error in a product/quotient adds
methods: Check dimensional consistency before trusting a derived formula
Count significant figures using the standard zero-counting rules
traps: Treating significant figures rules for addition/subtraction same as for multiplication/division
Confusing precision (least count) with accuracy
hard_archetypes: Combined percentage-error numericals across a multi-quantity formula (e.g. g from a pendulum)
banned_easy_templates: Bare 'state the SI unit of X' with no error/dimension reasoning
out_of_scope: Formal propagation-of-uncertainty statistics beyond NCERT treatment

concepts: Vector resolution and addition
Relative velocity in 1D/2D

Uniform circular motion centripetal acceleration

methods: Split projectile motion into independent horizontal/vertical components
Draw a relative-velocity vector diagram before computing river-boat/rain-man problems
traps: Mixing up angle of projection measured from horizontal vs vertical
Sign errors when velocity reverses direction in a v-t graph area calculation
hard_archetypes: Two-projectile relative-motion problems (collision/closest-approach)
Graph-based question requiring area-under-curve to get displacement, not just reading value
banned_easy_templates: Plug numbers into range formula with no twist
out_of_scope: Non-uniform circular motion with full tangential+radial vector treatment beyond NCERT depth

concepts: Newton's laws, free-body diagrams
Static vs kinetic friction
Circular motion dynamics (banking, conical pendulum)
methods: Always draw a free-body diagram before applying Newton's second law along an axis
Resolve forces along/perpendicular to an incline before writing equations
traps: Using μ_s where μ_k is needed once motion has started
Forgetting normal reaction changes on an accelerating lift/wedge
hard_archetypes: Connected-block-on-incline-with-pulley numericals needing simultaneous equations
Banking-of-road problems combined with friction (max/min speed range)
banned_easy_templates: Single block, single force, solve for acceleration with no constraint
out_of_scope: Non-inertial frame pseudo-force problems beyond a simple lift/wedge case

concepts: Work-energy theorem
Conservative force and potential energy
Elastic vs inelastic collisions
methods: Use energy conservation instead of kinematics when the path is complex but only endpoints matter
Identify collision type from given 'e' before choosing the momentum+energy equation set
traps: Applying KE conservation to an inelastic collision
Forgetting potential energy reference-point consistency across a problem

Multi-body collision + energy-loss numericals
banned_easy_templates: Direct KE = ½mv^2 substitution with no further reasoning
out_of_scope: Centre-of-mass frame collision analysis beyond lab-frame NCERT treatment

concepts: Centre of mass of discrete/continuous bodies
Torque and angular momentum conservation
Moment of inertia, parallel/perpendicular axis theorems
Rolling without slipping condition v=ωR
formulas: I = Σmr^2 (standard MoI list: ring, disc, sphere, rod)

Apply angular momentum conservation when external torque is zero (e.g. person on rotating platform)

Wrong axis when applying perpendicular-axis theorem (only valid for planar laminas)

Composite-body centre-of-mass problems (disc with a cut-out section)
banned_easy_templates: Direct MoI lookup for a standard body with no combination step
out_of_scope: Full rigid-body Euler-angle dynamics beyond NCERT scope

concepts: Newton's law of gravitation
Variation of g with height/depth/latitude
Escape velocity, orbital velocity

Sign errors in gravitational PE (always negative, reference at infinity)

Geostationary-satellite height derivation combined with Kepler's law
banned_easy_templates: Direct substitution into F = GMm/r^2 with no follow-up

de Broglie wavelength of matter
